analysis.objective: Design, implement, test, publish, and deploy a secure customer-facing web portal.
coreCapabilities: Customer registration, sign-in, sign-out, and password recovery
Health checks, telemetry, and error reporting
securityRequirements: Use managed identities and avoid credentials in source control
Store necessary secrets in Azure Key Vault or protected GitHub environments
Enforce HTTPS, secure cookies, authorization checks, and least-privilege access
Validate all input and protect sensitive customer data
Enable dependency, code, and secret scanning
Separate development, staging, and production configuration
assumptions: The GitHub organization or account and Azure subscription will be supplied
Authorized access will be available for repository and Azure resource creation
Detailed branding, data fields, user roles, and integrations will be confirmed before implementation
Production deployment will require an approval gate
No repository or Azure resources should be created until names, region, budget, and access are confirmed
successCriteria: The portal passes automated tests and security checks
The GitHub repository contains reviewed source code, documentation, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure definitions
The staging deployment passes smoke, authentication, database, and health checks
The production deployment is repeatable and protected by approval
A failed deployment produces sufficient diagnostics to identify, fix, and verify its root cause

actions: Confirm personas, workflows, roles, data model, branding, compliance needs, service-level objectives, Azure region, and budget
Define acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements
Create architecture, threat model, wireframes, and API contracts
Create a private GitHub repository using the approved organization and naming convention
Initialize the application, formatter, linter, test frameworks, commit conventions, and documentation
Configure branch protection, pull-request reviews, CODEOWNERS, Dependabot, code scanning, and secret scanning
Add environment-specific GitHub environments with staging and production approval rules
Build the responsive portal shell and reusable design system
Integrate Microsoft Entra External ID
Implement profile, dashboard, support request, and document workflows
Create database schema, migrations, authorization policies, validation, and audit events
Add accessible error, loading, empty, and session-expiry states
Add unit, integration, end-to-end, accessibility, and smoke tests
Run static analysis, dependency scanning, secret scanning, and container or package vulnerability checks
Validate authorization boundaries, input handling, session security, and privacy controls
Define release acceptance thresholds and rollback criteria
Define resource groups, App Service plan, web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault, managed identity, Application Insights, Log Analytics, networking, and alerts in Bicep
Configure staging and production parameters without embedding secrets
Grant least-privilege access between services
Add health endpoints, deployment slots where appropriate, backup policies, and retention settings
Configure pull-request validation for linting, type checking, tests, build, and security scans
Configure authenticated Azure deployment through GitHub OpenID Connect
Provision or update staging infrastructure, apply database migrations safely, and deploy the application
Run post-deployment health, smoke, authentication, and database connectivity checks
Require approval before production deployment and use a slot swap or controlled rollout where supported
Capture the failed workflow stage, deployment operation ID, timestamps, commit SHA, and affected environment
Inspect GitHub Actions logs, Azure Activity Log, deployment logs, App Service logs, Application Insights traces, health metrics, and database diagnostics
Classify the failure as authentication, authorization, infrastructure, configuration, build, migration, startup, networking, quota, runtime, or health-check related
Reproduce the failure in staging with sanitized configuration when possible
Apply the smallest reviewed fix to code, configuration, infrastructure, permissions, or migration logic
Rerun automated checks and redeploy to staging
Verify telemetry, health checks, core journeys, data integrity, and rollback readiness before production promotion
Document the root cause, contributing factors, resolution, and preventive controls
deliverables: Preventive test, alert, or runbook update
